open EuclideanGeometry

namespace Erdos93

/--
If $n$ distinct points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ form a convex polygon then they determine at least
$\lfloor \frac{n}{2}\rfloor$ distinct distances.

Solved by Altman [Al63].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 52, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/1d7b3f00780b85ed0462e79a1cd5650ee9055655/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos93.lean"]
theorem erdos_93 (A : Finset ℝ²) (hA : ConvexIndep (A : Set ℝ²)) :
    A.card / 2 ≤ distinctDistances A := by
  sorry

end Erdos93

reformulations.difference: The theorem uses A.card as n and permits all cardinalities, whereas a polygon ordinarily has at least three vertices and the cited formal proof explicitly assumes 3 ≤ n.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For cardinalities 0 and 1, the required floor(card/2) is zero. Two distinct points determine exactly one distance, meeting the required bound of one. Thus adding 3 ≤ A.card and an explicit n with A.card = n does not change the universal claim. In /workspace/review/scratch.lean I proved this equivalence and the equivalence with the linked proof's formulation: its ConvexIndependent predicate equals ConvexIndep, and its filtered-product distance image equals distanceSet. The equivalence proof does not use erdos_93 and has only standard Lean axioms.

review.notes:
The original 1946 and 1957 statements match the theorem. Checked the Euclidean metric, convex-position hypothesis, universal quantifiers, natural-number floor division, exclusion of zero distances, deduplication of equal distances, and small cardinalities. Lean tests also establish non-vacuity using subsets of the unit circle. Later Erdős papers attribute the solution to Altman, and the community status database records 'proved (Lean)', consistent with the metadata. The linked proof contains no sorry or custom axiom declarations; its statement was checked, but its full Lean 4.29.1 proof was not independently rebuilt.

Access limitations: erdosproblems.com/93 and the publisher/JSTOR copies of Altman's paper were blocked; text-mirror attempts also failed. The redundant later references Er90, Er92e, Er95, Er97e, and Er97f were not retrieved. Faithfulness was nevertheless settled against the original cited papers and the accessible later accounts. All scratch checks compile without errors, and the reviewed file matches the specified commit.
